title: Working backwards
examples: Teacher, if I know the answer, how do I find the first number?
Can we use this method for time problems too?
Does this only work for addition and subtraction?

explain.say: Today we learn to work backwards in math. This is useful when we know the end answer. We need to undo the steps that were done.
If you start with a number and add five, then take away two, you get a final number. To work backwards, you must do the opposite actions.
The opposite of adding five is subtracting five. The opposite of taking away two is adding two. We reverse the order too.
Let us try an example. If we start with ten, add five, then take away two. We get thirteen. Working backwards from thirteen, we add two to get fifteen. Then we subtract five to get ten.

faq.q: If I know the final amount, how do I find the starting amount?
faq.a: You must use the reverse operation for every step. If the last step was multiplying, you must divide to go back.
asks: How do I find the beginning number?
What is the opposite of multiplication?

faq.q: Does working backwards always mean doing the opposite math?
faq.a: Yes, it means doing the inverse operation. Addition undoes subtraction, and division undoes multiplication.
asks: Is it always the opposite math?
What is the inverse of subtraction?

faq.q: If I work backwards, do I change the order of the steps?
faq.a: Yes, you must reverse the order of the operations. You start with the last step and undo it first.
asks: Which way do I start working?

faq.q: Can I use this method if there are more than two steps?
faq.a: You can use it for any number of steps. Just remember to reverse the order and use the opposite operation for each one.
asks: Does this work for many steps?
How many steps can I undo?

faq.q: What if the problem uses money and I work backwards?
faq.a: Treat the money amounts like any other numbers. If you added money to get the total, you must subtract to find what was there before.
asks: Money problems work the same way?
Can I use this with currency?

facts: The opposite of addition is subtraction.
The opposite of subtraction is addition.
The opposite of multiplication is division.
To work backwards, you must reverse the order of operations.

quiz.say: A baker started with some cakes. He added five more cakes. Then he sold two cakes. If he has ten cakes now, how many did he start with?
quiz.why: We work backwards from ten. First, undo the selling two, so we add two to get twelve. Then, undo adding five by subtracting five to get seven. So he started with seven cakes.

wrong.0: This answer incorrectly adds five and two to ten, which is adding everything together.
wrong.1: This answer only adds two to ten and forgets to undo the initial addition of five.
wrong.2: This answer assumes no changes happened and just gives the final number.

quiz.say: A number was first multiplied by three. Then, five was subtracted. If the result is twenty-five, what was the original number?
quiz.why: We work backwards from twenty-five. First, undo subtracting five by adding five to get thirty. Then, undo multiplying by three by dividing by three to get ten. The original number was ten.

wrong.0: This answer incorrectly divides twenty-five by three and then adds five.
wrong.2: This answer only adds five to twenty-five, forgetting to undo the multiplication.
wrong.3: This answer correctly adds five but then incorrectly subtracts three from thirty.

quiz.say: If a total of forty-two was reached after first dividing a number by six, and then adding ten, what was the original number?
quiz.why: We work backwards from forty-two. First, undo adding ten by subtracting ten to get thirty-two. Then, undo dividing by six by multiplying by six to get one hundred ninety-two. Wait, let us recheck the steps. Forty-two minus ten is thirty-two. Thirty-two times six is one hundred ninety-two. Let us assume the starting number was 36. 36 divided by 6 is 6. 6 plus 10 is 16. Let us re-read the question. If the result is forty-two. Undo adding ten: forty

wrong.0: This answer only subtracts five from seventeen, forgetting to undo the division.
wrong.1: This answer correctly subtracts five from seventeen to get twelve, and then divides by three to get four. This is incorrect.
wrong.3: This answer incorrectly subtracts five from seventeen and then divides by three.
